name: /sdd:converge --behaviour: finds the unmet criterion the path check confirmed

graders.why: the point of criterion IDs is that a finding can name one. A report saying the limit is unhandled without citing AC2 leaves the reader to work out which requirement is unmet, which is the state this whole phase set out to end

the parameter is accepted and discarded, so the gap is partial or contradicts depending on how strictly you read it. Either is defensible; neither missing nor unrequested is, and a finding with no gap type is not classified at all
AC1 is genuinely met: list_widgets() returns all four. A run that flags both criteria has not checked either, and a fixture where everything is broken would hide that
graders.violating_example: 1.01/AC1 missing: nothing implements the widget listing

graders.why: a finding with no evidence is the command guessing, and it arrives in the same format as a measured one. The file or the function has to be named

graders.must_not_match: (?i)(I (have )?(updated|edited|reopened|changed) the task file|status (has been|was) (changed|updated|flipped)|marked it (in progress|not started))
graders.why: converge proposes and waits, which was a deliberate choice against manufacturing confident claims. The behavioural pass keeps it, and its evidence is weaker than the path check's, not stronger
graders.violating_example: I have updated the task file: Status is now In Progress.
